decision: On-demand CLI trigger only (no background daemon). Search via gh search repos, filtered by stars + pushed-within-2-years recency. One LLM call reads README + top-level dir structure per candidate repo, extracts transferable architecture patterns as prose (never verbatim code blocks). License fetched via gh repo view --json licenseInfo, copyleft (GPL/AGPL/LGPL) flagged prominently in output — non-negotiable per risk-auditor seat. Findings written as Markdown files into a folder registered as a docdb root, so results become FTS+semantic searchable without building a separate database.

stances.view: On-demand only, star+recency ranking, flat markdown storage, simple license print+flag. Objection: no serendipitous discovery outside explicit queries.

Top risks: silent license violations (most likely to bite), GitHub rate-limit exhaustion from background scanning, stale/bad patterns from star-only ranking, storage corruption, summaries hiding tradeoffs.

Build a compounding local pattern corpus (SQLite/docdb-backed) with project-aware query inference and structural quality signals beyond stars. Objection to self: structural scoring could be confidently wrong, and one user may never reach density to justify the complexity.

openQuestions: Project-aware auto-inference of search topic from cwd package.json was proposed by deep-reasoner and adopted as a cheap optional addition, not full structural scoring.

topic: build order for personal agent-tooling backlog (Knowledge/Infra/Autonomy/Orchestration)
decision: Reject strict category-sequencing (Knowledge then Infra then Autonomy then Orchestration last). Sort by actual dependency graph instead. Concrete order: (1) thin event log slice of Database (append-only feedback/error/repair/approve-reject table, NOT the full code-symbol-index which is a separate larger project overlapping the LSP/AST roadmap item), (2) static hand-written Model routing hook (cheap, high-leverage, do not wait for learned/adaptive routing), (3) Watchdog, (4) a lightweight Adversarial-review pass -- both 3 and 4 must exist before Autopilot per the users own never-grade-your-own-homework and verification-must-keep-pace-with-capability doctrine, (5) Blackboard (cheap, unblocks Council and session recovery). THEN Taste-distill and Dream (they are downstream consumers of logged history, not independent Knowledge-tier items). THEN Self-learning/Evolve, then Autopilot. Heavy orchestration (Godly-ultracode, Medtech-build-everything, Task-infra-audit) correctly stays last -- all seats agree on this part. Note: most orchestration primitives (task lifecycle, tool self-discovery, per-agent memory, inter-agent messaging, structured output, Council itself) are already shipped, so orchestration-last only applies to the remaining expensive tail, not the whole category.

stances.view: Build only the event-log slice of Database now, then pause and use the system before committing to any further sequence -- avoid pre-planning four tiers for a solo project with no forcing function.
Watchdog must precede or accompany Autopilot, not follow it -- shipping Autopilot before verification exists poisons self-learning training data and violates the users own stated doctrine.

Category-axis sequencing is the bug; sort by dependency and multiplier instead. Model routing and a thin event log are wave 0. Database as commonly meant conflates two different projects. Orchestration premise is already partly falsified since most primitives are shipped.

Keep the overall Knowledge-then-Infra-then-Autonomy-then-Orchestration shape but carve Model routing out to build early, since it directly serves the users own stated number one priority and is cheap/low-dependency unlike its orchestration bucket-mates.

openQuestions: Unresolved values call presented back to the user: how much of this sequence to commit to upfront (explicit multi-wave roadmap) vs. build the event log and router, then pause and let next steps emerge from real usage/pain (the pragmatist seats preferred cadence). Also unresolved: whether Research stays cut/deprioritized as flagged in the source material.

topic: whether to wire the destructive-command guard and config-protection hook live into settings.json
decision: Wire both live now. 3 of 4 seats favored wiring destructiveguard (status quo under bypassPermissions is zero protection, not a safe default; 66 tests + independent re-verification; asymmetric revert cost). The dissenting risk-auditor seat raised a real concern -- a hook with a documented blind spot (does not parse command substitution/subshells) wired silently could create false confidence, converting fail-open into fail-invisibly. Addressed that concretely rather than overriding it: baked the coverage-gap statement directly into the hook's own deny message, so the limitation is restated every time it fires rather than buried in a README. Deep-reasoner seat additionally found that the assumed precedent (always ask before wiring any hook) did not actually exist -- the model-routing hook already runs live without per-instance confirmation; only the autopilot Stop-gate was held back, for a different reason (trap risk, not deny risk). On configguard specifically the seats were tied 2-2; resolved via the same blast-radius/reversibility principle that decided destructiveguard (config-protection only touches 9 named filenames, does not touch Bash at all, and is at least as cheaply reversible), judged inconsistent to hold back the lower-risk hook while wiring the higher-risk one. Both hooks live-tested after wiring: destructiveguard denied a real rm -rf attempt before execution; configguard denied a real Edit attempt on an existing .eslintrc.json while allowing first-time creation via Write.

stances.view: Wire both now -- the counterfactual under bypassPermissions is zero protection, not caution; tests already exceed normal scrutiny; user explicitly asked for autonomous resolution of exactly this kind of question.

Leave both opt-in -- a documented blind spot (command substitution) wired live without a prompt risks false confidence, which is worse than an honestly-unguarded status quo the user consciously chose (bypassPermissions).

Split the two: wire destructiveguard (near-universal invariant, cheaply reversible, no actual always-ask precedent exists -- verified a live hook already runs unconfirmed today) but hold configguard (encodes an unarticulated filename preference, not a universal invariant). Flagged that a partial safety net can shift the constrained agent's own vigilance downward by more than it blocks -- mitigated by restating the coverage gap in the deny message itself.

Wire both now -- the user directly said stop asking this exact class of question in response to being asked exactly this; they already validated the underlying risk model as real, not hypothetical; asymmetric cost (one-line revert vs. another session's exposure).

openQuestions: Risk auditor's core objection (partial coverage breeding false confidence) was mitigated, not eliminated -- worth revisiting if the guard is ever seen to miss a real destructive command in practice, since that would confirm rather than merely hypothesize the false-confidence failure mode.

topic: local agent/workflow control-plane dashboard: build plan
decision: Build a minimal custom local Node.js+React app (not adopt LangGraph Studio/AutoGen Studio/Langflow/n8n, per prior deep-research). Data layer: a NEW separate SQLite db, not an extension of eventlog/claude.db -- eventlog's graded_by CHECK(IN ('human')) constraint is a load-bearing invariant (only human-graded rows) that a dashboard's high-volume ungraded telemetry would silently erode. Ingestion: tail existing ~/.claude/projects/**/*.jsonl transcripts + blackboard NDJSON + poll model-routing.json/modelweighter metrics -- no new hooks in the hot path (already 6 wired). v1 scope: read-only core (agent/run timeline, deliverables, model-routing rationale panel including modelweighter metrics) PLUS one narrow, foreground-only interactive action (pick a role+model tier, dispatch a prompt, stream output live, no background job queue) and a model-tier override form -- but any write to model-routing.json must go through a validated atomic-write function, never a raw overwrite, since a malformed write silently degrades routing for all future Agent calls with no crash (fail-open hooks mean silent failure, not safe failure -- unanimous concern across all 4 seats). Deferred to v2, pending verification: persistent live chat via `claude -p --resume`/stream-json with a dashboard-spawned agent (mechanically real and cheap, verified empirically by the deep-reasoner seat, but needs a check first that existing PreToolUse hooks still fire correctly on a headless -p-spawned session the way they do interactively); background task queue/status polling; interactive graph auto-layout/editing. Side-finding surfaced during this council, independent of the dashboard decision: modelweighter's learned-belief layer has NEVER fired in production (0 promoted beliefs, 0 feedback rows) -- the static keyword table has done 100% of routing since it was built. Not necessarily a bug (promotion requires human grading via a CLI nobody's been running), but a real gap worth closing -- a "grading inbox" UI is a strong v2 dashboard feature specifically because it turns this dormant infrastructure into a working one.

stances.view: Extend eventlog (later corrected by other seats' finding re: the graded_by invariant); tail transcripts/blackboard, no new hooks; ship strictly read-only v1 (status+map+deliverables), defer chat and model-reassignment entirely to v1.1; if chat ships at all, label it honestly as "compose a new task prefilled with context," not live chat.

Separate SQLite db to protect eventlog's human-graded invariant; tail transcripts/blackboard, no 7th hook; ship strictly read-only v1, defer ALL write-actions; flagged the concrete failure mode that a malformed model-routing.json write fails open (silent, not crashing) and could unroute all Agent calls to full-cost models for days before anyone notices; live chat needs hook-refire-on-resume verified before shipping. (First run of this seat was hard-denied by this project's own route-enforcer hook, matching on the literal phrase "risk audit" -- re-run with the [claude-required] override marker.)

Empirically verified (not just argued) that live bidirectional chat with a dashboard-spawned agent is mechanically real and cheap via `claude -p --input-format stream-json` (true duplex, ~1.5s follow-up turns) and `-p --resume <session-id>` from a fresh process. Also discovered modelweighter's learning loop has never fired in production (0 promoted beliefs) -- argued the dashboard's highest-value v1 feature is a grading inbox that closes that loop, not a workflow graph. Recommended framing agents as ROLES (identity+model tier+session lineage) rather than PROCESSES, since Claude Code has no long-lived agent processes -- a role's memory is just its session transcript, resumed via --resume. Self-flagged objection: a frictionless chat UI cuts directly against the user's stated #1 priority (cost minimization) -- measured a single haiku "OK" reply at $0.026 due to full system-prompt resend; recommended defaulting chat to the local/ free cascade with explicit escalation to spend real Claude tokens, and showing cost-per-turn inline.

Argued strict read-only v1 under-delivers on the user's literal, explicit ask (interactable, prompt my agents, assign tasks, pick models) -- proposed the middle ground: read-only visibility plus one narrow real interactive slice (foreground-only prompt dispatch via the Agent-tool mental model the user already has, plus a model-tier override form wrapping the existing model-routing.json/modelweighter config, never replacing it). Self-flagged objection: "narrow interactivity" is the exact seam where scope creeps, since task-dispatch-with-status-tracking is a background job system in disguise -- recommended explicitly cutting background/async dispatch from v1 and keeping it foreground-only.

openQuestions: How much v1 interactivity to accept was a genuine values/risk-tolerance fork (pragmatist+risk-auditor: none; deep-reasoner+user-advocate: some) resolved via synthesis (one narrow foreground-only action) rather than picked for the user -- worth confirming they're comfortable with that cut before building. Also open: whether the dormant modelweighter learning loop is worth fixing on its own regardless of the dashboard's timeline.

topic: solo bootstrapped autonomous Claude-built business targeting $1M/month net income
decision: Reject original pick (AR/collections automation for accounting firms) and reject legal/healthcare/insurance/recruiting verticals entirely - regulatory licensing requires a human decision-maker, incompatible with autonomy goal and the users own standing no-autonomous-irreversible-action rule. Converge on an autonomy-compatible self-serve model. Primary recommendation: agent-operated proprietary-data/API-and-alerts business (collect-normalize-publish changing datasets, sold via metered API+alerts to businesses, $200-2000/mo), run as a portfolio of multiple boring verticals on one shared platform once built - chosen for moat (owned data history vs rentable content/traffic) and low per-error stakes. Alternative fork: productize the users own existing agent-orchestration tool stack as a self-serve dev-tools SaaS - lower build cost, matches revealed behavior pattern, but weaker moat/more crowded category. All four seats agree literal zero-human perfect autonomy is not achievable at this revenue scale - soften to no salespeople ever, <=5 FTE none in sales, human retained only at legal/compliance/pricing choke points.

stances.view: Self-serve usage-metered API/infrastructure product for developers as flagship, content/affiliate as small parallel bet not main vehicle. Flags tension: top accounts in usage-based businesses often need a sales-assisted tier to capture revenue concentration, which could cap ARR if autonomy is held rigidly.

Legal/healthcare/insurance/AR-collections/regulated-marketplace all ruled out on licensing grounds - autonomous decision-making in those spaces is often flatly illegal, not just risky. PLG software, API/infra, and FTC-compliant content are the safe set. Recommends hybrid: full autonomy in day-to-day ops, human retained at sales/strategic layer only.

Reframe filter as judgment-decisions-per-dollar, not self-serve-vs-sales. Quantifies content/affiliate as needing 2-3 orders of magnitude more traffic than a data/API subscription model for same net income, and flags Google scaled-content-abuse policy risk. Recommends proprietary-data/API-and-alerts portfolio business - moat compounds as owned historical data, agents make marginal-vertical cost near zero once platform exists so a solo founder can stack many $1-5M ARR verticals. Names data-acquisition legal risk (ToS/CFAA/licensing) as the real remaining human-judgment residue; mitigate via government/licensed sources and hard-excluding FCRA-adjacent verticals (credit, insurance, tenant screening, employment).

Recommends productizing the users own existing agent-orchestration stack (docdb, model routing, agentic coding loop) as a self-serve PLG dev-tools SaaS - matches revealed behavior pattern of bounded reversible autonomy with a hard stop at irreversible actions. Advises bending the revenue target/timeline rather than the autonomy boundary, since the autonomy rule is a considered standing principle and the $1M number is aspirational. Flags dev-tools category as crowded/low-moat, a real cost of this pick.

openQuestions: Which fork does the user actually want: build a new proprietary-data/alerts business optimized for moat and ARR ceiling (higher build effort, new domain, some data-acquisition legal risk) vs productize the tool stack already built (lower effort, matches current workflow, weaker competitive moat)? Also open: whether the user accepts softening zero-human to <=5 FTE/no-salespeople-ever as the working definition of autonomous.

topic: build order + autonomy boundary for self-improving Claude stack (watchdog widening, folder-check, auto session-drift, idea-proposal system) under parallel blackboard-coordinated build
decision: Adopt a single converged recommendation (all 4 seats landed close together after investigation, not a values fork). (A) Auto-execution: never on settings.json, hook-wiring, deny-list files (destructiveguard/configguard/envguard), or anything outside ~/.claude -- unanimous, worst case is total hook-system failure on next session start. Ephemeral/cosmetic maintenance (cache invalidation, log cleanup, docdb index rebuild) can auto-execute now. A narrow middle tier -- bounded to tools/** or skills/**, shipped as a git-revertible wake-builder nightly-branch commit, and self-verifying (ships with a check that failed before and passes after) -- may auto-execute, but only inside the nightly batch job, never mid-session, and only after the belief-promotion loop has a verified non-poisoned track record. (B) Parallel build: reject naive 1-team-per-item (4 teams). Adopt single-integrator pattern -- no spawned team edits settings.json directly; teams post wiring requests to blackboard, orchestrator applies one serialized edit at the end. Partition into 3 teams by file ownership: T1 = items 1+2 merged (same watchdog file, not parallel-safe if split) building tools/watchdog into a general stack-health + folder-correctness sweep; T2 = item 3, wires a new SessionStart hook key (does not yet exist in settings.json) to fire sessionrecovery's rollup automatically; T3 replaces the originally-proposed net-new idea-proposal inbox -- deep-reasoner found the enforcement/selflearning belief-promotion pipeline is already live (wired into 2 of 9 hooks) but poisoned by a real bug (pending.jsonl has 23 lines / 6 distinct toolUseIds, no dedup, meaning 3x-duplicated single observations can falsely cross the promotion threshold and silently override live model routing) and starved (10 ungraded autopilot decisions, only 5 grades ever logged, all positive, one human-CLI grading step nobody runs). T3's job: fix the dedup bug first (urgent, actively at risk of corrupting live routing), then collapse the human-grading gate to one batched one-keystroke SessionStart prompt (riding T2's new hook) instead of a separate CLI, with derived/exogenous observations (edits kept vs reverted, turn errored, task re-spawned) allowed to pre-fill a suggested verdict but never auto-promote on their own -- preserves the eventlog graded_by human-only invariant a prior council already ruled load-bearing.

stances.view: No auto-exec until trust is earned from real proposal history; split parallel work by file contention not item-count; merge items 1+2 since same file; sequence anything touching settings.json rather than risk a race.

Auto-exec only for cosmetic/ephemeral non-config changes; worst-case blast radius of a settings.json race is total hook-system failure on next session start (autopilot/watchdog/gates all silently stop loading); fix the live dedup bug before anything else executes.

Reversible-vs-irreversible is the wrong predicate on a git-backed personal tool directory; replaced it with a 3-part conjunctive test (bounded blast radius, pre-committed git-revertible undo, self-verifying). Found the belief-promotion pipeline is live-but-poisoned, not dormant, and argued closing that loop is higher-leverage than building a new proposal inbox that would terminate in the same unresponsive human. Self-flagged that derived/exogenous verdicts risk eroding the eventlog human-only invariant -- conceded to a pre-fill-only, never-auto-promote fallback.

User's 'everything automatic' most plausibly means automate detection/triggering (fully solved by items 1-3), not remove the one approval gate in a plan they just called good -- a boundary reaffirmed by a separate council the same day is not overridden by a dictated aside without stronger signal. Recommended stating the kept gate plainly rather than silently keeping it, so the user can override in one line if this reading is wrong. On parallelism: verify actual file collision before forcing a team merge rather than assuming from names alone.

openQuestions: Whether the user wants the auto-execute middle tier enabled immediately once T3's dedup fix + first honest promoted belief lands, or wants to observe the health-sweep's proposal history for a while first before granting even the narrow tools/**-only auto-exec tier. Also open: a 2026-07-31 council already designed a local control-plane dashboard (read-only v1 + one foreground interactive slice) that was never built -- worth folding into this build queue as a 4th track or treated as separate.

topic: user override of settings.json human-gate + build-system autonomy scope (supersedes earlier decision same day)
decision: User explicitly overrode this session's earlier 4-seat council finding after being told the concrete risk in plain terms (a bad hook-wiring write can silently disable every hook with no live recovery path). Chosen tier: full autonomy including settings.json itself, no human checkpoint anywhere in the new build systems. This is a user decision, not a council synthesis -- logged for precedent/traceability, not as a re-litigated consensus. Implementation response: rather than remove the safety property entirely, moved it from a human-approval gate to an automatic self-verifying gate -- tools/settingswriter (T10) becomes the sole path for future settings.json changes, validates JSON/file-existence/syntax after every write and auto-rolls-back on failure with no human involvement either way. On the separate 'unrestricted full PC access' ask: NOT granted as literally unrestricted -- held a hard line (stated to the user as a factual security concern, not a negotiated preference) that an unattended, internet-reading, scheduled agent with zero tool restriction is a live prompt-injection/RCE vector. User did not push back on that specific point. Compromise implemented: substantially widened tool/directory allowlists for wake-agent/wake-builder/localmodel (T10 part B), keeping exactly three fixed lines -- no credential/secret access, no destructive ops outside ~/.claude and tracked project repos, everything git-revertible.

stances.view: Explicit, informed choice after seeing the concrete failure mode spelled out via AskUserQuestion options: 'auto-apply literally everything, including settings.json' selected over the recommended safer tier and the status-quo-gate tier.

openQuestions: Whether this precedent should generalize to future settings.json-touching work by default, or was scoped to this session's specific build systems. Also open: the user has not yet responded to the specific prompt-injection/RCE reasoning for holding the line on literal unrestricted PC access -- worth confirming they accept that boundary rather than assuming silence is agreement.

decision: v1 = staged/earned autonomy, not full access. No-ask: reads/research/scoring/scratch-worktree work (docdb, ghscan, deep-research, evolve trials). Must-confirm: anything touching credentials/auth, email, git push, cron/scheduling, settings.json/permissions/hooks, file deletion, changes outside ~/.claude, and any change to the guardrails/scorer/promotion-logic itself. Rollback gate: git-tracked change + cascade-verify/tests must pass before any auto-apply; canary/shadow-run promotion as a later rung once a class of change has a clean track record, not v1. Cadence: session/manual-triggered for v1, NOT a cron daemon or always-on loop -- matches how this user actually works (bursts, not server-mode); event-driven or scheduled batch is a v2 option once trust is earned. Scorers: reuse existing instrumentation (cascade tier logs, evolve keep-if-better, efficiency/analyze.js) rather than inventing new ones; quality must be judged by something other than the model/loop that produced the change (held-out tasks / separate judge / occasional human spot-check), hard constraints not a single weighted sum, to resist Goodharting speed/token metrics. Full literal hands-off access explicitly NOT granted for v1 -- open question put back to the user.

stances.view: Bounded propose-then-diff loop; no-ask only for reads/scratch-worktree trials; must-confirm for anything touching live prompts/configs/permissions/deps/its own cadence; scorers must be graded by a separate judge, not self-graded; expand scope only after clean cycles build trust.

Deny full access; v1 = research-and-propose only. Blast radius from email/credentials/git is unrecoverable at scale (spam, leaked creds, public bad commits). Self-modifying scorers decay into metric gaming within weeks. Loop researching online is a supply-chain attack surface on itself (malicious repo/blog could be applied as truth).

Build a promotion ladder, not a static permission list -- autonomy earned per action-class via measured track record (shadow-run then canary then full). Guardrails/scorer/permission logic must be a boundary the loop itself cannot edit. Event-driven triggers (new sources found, pattern threshold, scorer regression) beat fixed cron. Scorers as hard constraints with an unpredictable human spot-check, not a weighted sum a model can game.

Grant broad autonomy on the execute-and-verify loops already trusted (routing/cascade, evolve/recalibrate/ghscan passes) now; withhold literal full-access hands-off for v1. Session-triggered cadence fits this user's actual burst usage, not a daemon. Reuse existing scorers instead of inventing new ones. Do not unilaterally narrow scope on the user's behalf -- ask them directly what silent failure they'd regret most, since their own MVP-first pattern on autopilot suggests they'll self-scope once asked.

openQuestions: What's the one thing that, if it broke silently while the user was away, would make them regret granting broader autonomy? Answer determines how fast v1->v2->v3 scope expansion should move. Also unresolved: exact cadence mechanism for v2+ (scheduled batch vs event-driven) -- deferred until v1 has run enough cycles to have real signal.

topic: autonomy guardrails for self-optimizing stack - user override
decision: User explicitly expanded v1 scope beyond council recommendation: cron/scheduling changes, settings.json/hooks/permissions edits, and git push are now NO-ASK for the self-optimizing loop (previously recommended as must-confirm by all 4 council seats). Standing global git safety protocol (no force-push, no unsolicited push to main, no skipped hooks) is unaffected -- this override is about routine push/schedule/config authority, not a waiver of those separate hard rules. Still must-confirm pending user reply: credentials/auth file changes, email sending, file deletion outside ~/.claude, and changes to the guardrails/scorer/promotion logic itself.
openQuestions: Does the user want credentials/auth, email sending, and deletion outside ~/.claude to also move to no-ask, or do those remain the hard boundary? Awaiting explicit answer before treating silence as expansion.

decision: Built ~/.claude/tools/selfoptimize/ (config.json, lib.js, level0-run.js, level1-verify.js, nightly.bat, Startup-folder SelfOptimizeNightly.vbs). Level 0 = ghscan research + evolve overnight mutate/score loop (evolve already refuses to auto-adopt -- hard anti-rule in its own SKILL.md). Level 1 = independent re-check on a DIFFERENT model tier (localmodel reasoning tier, distinct from whatever evolve used) before the ONLY auto-adopt step in the whole pipeline: copy verified winner over the real original file (tracked via new original_path field added to autoresearch_init.py config output) + local git commit (no push -- see open question). Level 2 (/council anchor) is session-triggered, not scheduled -- see infra findings. Trust-weighting: selflearning.observe() (the shared auto-promoting Bayesian belief store) is reserved for deterministic-graded outcomes only, per its own hard never-grade-your-own-homework rule; LLM-judged outcomes log to llm-graded-observations.jsonl instead, visible but non-authoritative. Opt-in per evolve project via new selfoptimize:true config flag -- zero existing projects opted in yet (finetune-custom still overnight-only). Smoke-tested: --all discovery, config/boundary/trust plumbing all verified working with zero projects opted in (safe no-op).
openQuestions: Infra reality check that reshaped the build: (1) CronCreate is session-only, dies with the session (7-day max even recurring) -- cannot be Level 0/1 persistence. (2) The schedule skill's cloud routines run in an isolated Anthropic sandbox with NO access to local files/tools -- cannot invoke evolve/ghscan/localmodel/selflearning at all, only usable for a git-remote-mediated Level 2 anchor. (3) ~/.claude IS a local git repo but has NO remote configured -- the git-push authority the user granted has nothing to push to yet. Real open question for the user: set up a remote (new private repo? existing one?) to (a) make git push actually do something and (b) unlock a genuinely-independent cloud-routine Level 2 that cannot be gamed by anything running locally. Until then Level 2 stays session-triggered (I run /council when asked or when floorDays has elapsed and a session happens to start).
